recognize_zh: 血小板低下的男孩周邊血中，血小板體積大、呈淡灰藍色且幾乎看不到紫紅色顆粒（右圖放大），旁邊中性球顆粒正常，符合灰色血小板症候群（gray platelet syndrome，α 顆粒缺乏，NBEAL2 變異）。
features: Enlarged platelets, some approaching red cell size (macrothrombocytes)
Platelet cytoplasm is pale gray-blue and nearly devoid of azurophilic (alpha) granules
Platelet number reduced in the field
Neutrophil with normal granulation and segmentation, without Döhle-like inclusions
Red cells normochromic with a few showing mild shape variation
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows reduced platelets, many of which are enlarged, with pale gray-blue cytoplasm that is nearly devoid of azurophilic granules. The neutrophil present shows normal granulation and lacks Döhle-like inclusions, and red cells are largely unremarkable. These findings are consistent with gray platelet syndrome, an alpha-granule deficiency typically due to biallelic NBEAL2 variants; electron microscopy or immunofluorescence for alpha-granule proteins and genetic testing provide confirmation.

ddx.dx: Artifactual platelet degranulation (EDTA storage or poor staining)
ddx.vs: In-vitro degranulation affects platelets of normal size and is corrected on a fresh citrated smear, whereas GPS platelets are large and consistently agranular.
MYH9 disease has giant but normally granulated platelets and neutrophil Döhle-like inclusions.
BSS has giant granulated platelets with absent ristocetin agglutination due to GPIb-IX-V deficiency.
MDS shows hypogranular platelets alongside dysplastic neutrophils and other lineage abnormalities in an older patient.
